_what: Graceful's run-energy recovery, per piece. External facts first, then the departure Corey chose and the arithmetic that turns it into six whole numbers. Written before any config was edited; tools/outfit_battery checks in gamemode_battery.py group 64b read this file, so a number changed here without the config changing goes red, and vice versa.

osrs._note: Re-read rather than taken from the earlier round's notes, because this round rewrites the comment that states it.

departure._who: Corey, backlog item 5: "Graceful gives +50% energy recovery".
departure._replaces_not_adds: 50 is the new total, not 50 on top of the 20 it paid before. Asked and answered before anything was built.
departure._shape: The whole 50 comes from the pieces' own params, so a partial set pays its share and there is no full-set bonus at all. The alternative - OSRS's per-piece numbers plus a large set bonus - was offered and not chosen, and it would have cost the set mechanism the engine deliberately does not have: calculateRunWeight() sums a param over worn gear and knows nothing about which outfit a piece belongs to.
departure._osrs_set_bonus_dropped: OSRS's own +10% for all six is still not implemented and now does not need to be: the 50 already exceeds OSRS's 30 by twenty points, so a set bonus on top would be a departure on a departure.

scaling._factor: 50 / 20. Applied to OSRS's per-piece numbers so the relative shape survives: a 4% piece stays worth more than a 3% piece, in the same proportion.
scaling._rounding: 3 x 2.5 is 7.5, which is not a whole percent. The two 4% pieces land on 10 exactly. The four 3% pieces have to sum to 30, so two take 8 and two take 7.
scaling._tie_break: Which of the four take 8 is decided by the piece's own weight reduction, not by taste: boots and cape reduce 4 kg and take 8, hood and gloves reduce 3 kg and take 7. This is OSRS's own principle at a finer grain - its 4% pieces are its two heaviest reductions (-6 and -5) and its 3% pieces are the -4s and -3s - and it makes the result a checkable property rather than a choice: recovery is non-decreasing in weight reduction, and equal reductions get equal recovery.

result._engine: No engine change. calculateRunWeight() already sums the energy_restore param over worn equipment into runrestore, and updateEnergy() already scales natural recovery by it: natural + ((natural * runrestore) / 100 | 0).
